BiblicalUsage: Solomon's goldsmiths hammered this word into shields and targets of beaten gold, six hundred shekels to a target and three hundred to a shield. The king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon, where beaten gold hung as a sign of his glory.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe beaten gold tells the truth about Solomon's kingdom, that glory hammered thin still shines, but it cannot hold.
